title: Telemetry Stack With O(1) Minimum

visible.label: Push, min updates, and pop restores previous min
visible.inputDisplay: push(-2), push(0), push(-3), get_min(), pop(), top(), get_min()
visible.script:
st = MinStack()
st.push(-2)
st.push(0)
st.push(-3)
assert st.get_min() == -3
st.pop()
assert st.top() == 0
assert st.get_min() == -2

visible.label: Duplicate minimum values pop safely
visible.script:
st = MinStack()
st.push(5)
st.push(5)
assert st.get_min() == 5
assert st.pop() == 5
assert st.get_min() == 5

hidden.label: Decreasing then increasing wave
hidden.script:
st = MinStack()
st.push(10)
st.push(4)
st.push(8)
st.push(2)
assert st.get_min() == 2
st.pop()
assert st.get_min() == 4
st.pop()
assert st.get_min() == 4
st.pop()
assert st.get_min() == 10

hidden.label: Popping empty stack raises IndexError
Negative and zero minimum tracking
hidden.script:
st = MinStack()
st.push(0)
st.push(-1)
assert st.get_min() == -1
st.pop()
assert st.get_min() == 0

hidden.label: Single element cycle empty and reuse
hidden.script:
st = MinStack()
st.push(7)
assert st.pop() == 7
st.push(3)
assert st.get_min() == 3

hidden.label: O(1) per-operation performance under 20,000 get_min calls
hidden.expectedDisplay: All get_min queries execute in O(1)
hidden.script:
st = MinStack()
for x in range(15000, 0, -1):
    st.push(x)
    assert st.get_min() == x
for _ in range(5000):
    st.pop()
assert st.get_min() == 5001

hints: Each item pushed onto the stack freezes what the minimum was up to that depth.
Store tuples `(value, current_min)` on a single stack (or keep a parallel `mins` stack). On push, new_min = min(value, current_min).

Pseudocode:
  class MinStack:
      def __init__(self): self.data = []
      def push(self, x): cur = x if not self.data else min(x, self.data[-1][1]); self.data.append((x, cur))
      def pop(self): return self.data.pop()[0]
      def top(self): return self.data[-1][0]
      def get_min(self): return self.data[-1][1]
